concept: DatePicker is a text window with a round key beside it. The window is the same recess as Input and takes a typed date; the key is a real part that opens the Calendar on a small plastic panel, so a person can type the date they know or turn to a month and press the one they want.

default_to_avoid.pattern: date picker: a bordered input with a calendar icon trapped inside its edge and a masked mm/dd/yyyy template that eats every keystroke
default_to_avoid.why_not: The icon inside the field is a flat glyph with no mechanism and no edge of its own, and the rigid mask rejects a date typed in the format the person already knows.

default_to_avoid.pattern: native date input with its browser calendar popup
default_to_avoid.why_not: The browser draws its own popup in a second material and second language, so the display, the key and the panel stop belonging to one appliance.

references.source: Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): the entry window is a recess in the body, and the keys that fill it stand beside it as separate parts
Braun AB 20 quartz alarm clock (Dietrich Lubs, 1975): the setting wheel is its own part beside the dial it sets, never printed inside the dial
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, date picker combobox example: a text field with a button that opens a dialog holding the grid
system/FORM.md input class: recessed well, full width of its column, label printed above on the inset line

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The date window is surface.sunken with elevation.well, the same recess as Input, and it keeps its whole edge because the key stands outside it.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The label, the row of window and key, and the messages stack in one column with the label at the start edge above the window.
The calendar key is the round IconButton inside Popover with the schedule glyph, a separate raised part beside the recess instead of a mark printed in it.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: The window is control.md tall and the key is control.key square, so both share top and bottom edges on one row at 44px.

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: Focus is the shared dark ring and an invalid date is a red mark with a glyph and words, so the picker never spends the unit's orange.

options.name: raised round key sitting inside the window's end
full recessed window with the round key standing beside it
flat printed glyph behind a seam inside the window

variants.reason: B keeps the window a whole recess and the key a real raised part on the same row, so a typed date and a pressed key each look like what they are; A pushes a raised key out over the recess edge, and C prints a flat glyph that has no edge, reads as a second field and gives the 44px target no visible shape.

root.why: The picker stacks its label, its row and its messages in one column so the label sits on the inset line above the window.

label.why: The printed name uses the label size in medium weight, the same as Input, and is the accessible name of the text field.

row.why: The window and the key stand in one row at the same height with a gap between them, so their top and bottom edges line up.

well.why: The recess takes the inverse light, shade on its top-left inner edge, so the person sees where the date is typed.

field.why: The typed date is primary ink on the sunken plastic above 4.5:1, with tabular figures and a line box tall enough for Thai marks, and it fills the well so the whole 44px is its press area.

key.why: The Popover root that holds the round calendar key is held at its own width so the window takes all the spare room.

sheet.why: The Calendar stands centred in a fixed-width block on the panel so choosing a day or turning a month never moves the panel's contents.

hint.why: The hint prints the accepted format in secondary ink above 4.5:1 under the row, so it never covers the typed date.

error.why: The error message is a red mark with words, never the orange, which stays reserved for the unit's primary control.

glyph.why: A printed mark beside the words means an invalid date is never told by colour alone, for people who cannot see the red.

focus-within.why: The window shows the same dark ring as every part when the text field holds the keyboard focus.

data-invalid=true.why: An invalid window draws its edge in the critical red, which is never orange, and the message below says what to type.

data-disabled=true.why: A disabled picker loses its recess shadow and the text fades to half, and the key is switched off, so it reads as taking nothing now.

data-readonly=true.why: A read-only picker keeps the recess but shows a default cursor, because the date can be read and copied and cannot be changed.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the window keeps a real border and the focus ring uses the system highlight colour.
